verdictSummary: The C++26/WPF architecture is fast and well-structured, but a guaranteed std::terminate() crash on exit after playing White Noise (#1), Hangul P/Invoke buffer overflows (#2), settings data-loss paths (#3, #4), and an inverted screen-capture privacy check (#6) should be fixed before the next release.

findings.title: Closing the app after playing White Noise crashes the process via std::terminate()
findings.whatThisIs: The native background audio thread that generates and plays ambient white noise.
findings.problem: vn_noise_play starts g.thread = std::thread(PlayerThread), and vn_noise_stop sets g.wantOn = false without ever calling g.thread.join(). Even after the audio loop finishes, g.thread.joinable() stays true, so when the user exits V-Notch, the global PlayerState destructor destroys a joinable std::thread and C++ immediately calls std::terminate().
findings.fix: Join g.thread inside vn_noise_stop() (outside g.stateLock) and in PlayerState::~PlayerState(), and call WhiteNoiseService.Instance.Stop() during App.OnExit.
findings.consequenceIfSkipped: Every session where the user plays White Noise ends with an unhandled native abort() crash on app exit.

findings.title: Playing Korean tracks or searching multi-token queries crashes C# string marshalling with ArgumentOutOfRangeException
findings.whatThisIs: The C# to C++26 string normalization and search query builders used for media track matching and Spotlight search.
findings.problem: vnotch::copy_out_u16 writes the full required length into *out_len before returning VN_ERR_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL (-2). Five C# wrappers allocate fixed buffers (value.Length + 8 or span.Length * 2 + 16), ignore the return code (_ = vn_...), and call new string(buf, 0, outLen). Because NormalizeString(NormalizationD) expands each Korean Hangul syllable into up to 3 Jamo characters, any 5-syllable Korean artist like "방탄소년단" sets outLen = 14 against a buffer of length 13 and throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException.
findings.fix: Check the return code of vn_* in all string-returning C# wrappers; when it returns VN_ERR_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL (-2) and outLen > cap, allocate a char[outLen] buffer and retry the call.
findings.consequenceIfSkipped: Playing K-Pop or Korean media tracks, or typing wildcard-heavy queries in Spotlight, throws unhandled exceptions in media detection and search.

findings.title: A timed-out settings save during startup migration deletes the user's primary settings.json
findings.whatThisIs: The startup migration routine that encrypts legacy plaintext AI API keys in settings.json and cleans up plaintext backup files.
findings.problem: When LoadFromDisk() finds a plaintext API key, it calls Save(settings, keepExistingBackup: false) and then unconditionally runs RemovePlaintextKeySettingsFiles(). If ExecuteSave times out waiting for the cross-process mutex (!acquired at line 370), it returns silently without writing to disk. RemovePlaintextKeySettingsFiles() then scans Directory.GetFiles(_appFolder, "settings*.json") — which matches settings.json itself — sees the unmigrated plaintext key still inside settings.json, and deletes the user's primary settings file.
findings.fix: Exclude _settingsPath (settings.json) from RemovePlaintextKeySettingsFiles(), have ExecuteSave return a bool indicating whether the disk write succeeded, only clean up backup files when Save returns true, and serialize synchronous Save() with _saveChannel.
findings.consequenceIfSkipped: Any momentary file lock or second-instance contention during startup permanently deletes the user's settings.json.

findings.title: Opening a settings file from a newer app version wipes all user settings and encrypted API keys
findings.whatThisIs: The schema version check that runs whenever settings.json is loaded from disk.
findings.problem: When startVersion > CurrentVersion, SettingsMigrator.Migrate throws JsonException. SettingsService.LoadFromDisk catches JsonException as file corruption, renames settings.json to settings.corrupt-<timestamp>.json, and overwrites settings.json (keepExistingBackup: false) with blank defaults.
findings.fix: When startVersion > CurrentVersion, log a warning and return the parsed JsonObject as-is instead of throwing JsonException.
findings.consequenceIfSkipped: Rolling back an update or running an older build once wipes every user preference and encrypted API key.

findings.title: Importing a portable clipboard backup saves the secret vault pepper in plaintext on disk
findings.whatThisIs: The backup import function for the encrypted Personal Clipboard Vault.
findings.problem: ExportPortableConfig decrypts the DPAPI-protected vault pepper and prefixes it with "raw:" so it can move across machines. ImportPortableConfig writes that JSON straight to personal-key.json without re-encrypting the "raw:" pepper under ProtectedData.Protect(..., DataProtectionScope.CurrentUser) ("enc:") and without checking that config.Verification is at least 28 bytes.
findings.fix: Validate config.Verification is { Length: >= 28 }, decode the pepper via UnprotectPepper, re-protect it with ProtectPepper ("enc:"), and only then write personal-key.json.
findings.consequenceIfSkipped: After a backup restore, the master pepper stays in plaintext ("raw:") on disk forever, defeating Windows DPAPI protection.

findings.title: Enabling 'Hide From Screen Capture' actually exposes the notch during screenshots
findings.whatThisIs: The screen-capture privacy guard in the Liquid Glass rendering loop.
findings.problem: In HandleCaptureOverlay(), the guard if (!_hideFromCapture) return; is inverted: when _hideFromCapture is true and the user opens Snipping Tool or presses Win+Shift+S, the code falls through to line 986 and calls SetWindowDisplayAffinitySafe(WDA_NONE), removing capture protection at the exact moment a screenshot is taken. The same unguarded WDA_NONE call runs in SleepUntilRenderDeadline and WaitDeadlineSlice.
findings.fix: Change HandleCaptureOverlay() to if (_hideFromCapture) return; and guard the WDA_NONE calls in SleepUntilRenderDeadline and WaitDeadlineSlice with if (!_hideFromCapture).
findings.consequenceIfSkipped: Users who turn on 'Hide From Screen Capture' for privacy have their notch and media/clipboard contents captured in screenshots anyway.

findings.title: Native handle races and thread leaks in MagnifierCapture, MicrophoneProbe, and LoopbackCapture can corrupt memory (Use-After-Free)
findings.whatThisIs: The C++26 background capture engines for desktop magnification, microphone activity probing, and WASAPI audio loopback.
findings.problem: MagnifierCapture::Find returns an unleased raw Source* after releasing g_registry_lock, racing with vn_magcap_destroy (Use-After-Free), and Source::Start() leaks a running pump thread on 1500ms timeout. MicrophoneProbe mutates probe->entries across concurrent leases with no per-probe lock. LoopbackCapture zeroes thread_id before ~Capture() and drops self_delete if stopped from the callback thread while another lease is active.
findings.fix: Migrate MagnifierCapture and AudioDevices to HandleRegistry<T, 64> and call Stop() on Start() timeout; add a CriticalSection inside mp::Probe; and fix self_delete / thread_id ordering in LoopbackCapture.
findings.consequenceIfSkipped: Monitor hot-plugging, DPI changes, or audio device switches can trigger native access violations (0xC0000005) or leak Win32 pump threads.

findings.title: Unprotected heap allocations inside noexcept C ABI exports and 0.0 / 0.0 division in ArtworkFrameDetector
findings.whatThisIs: The C++26 VN_EXPORT ... noexcept boundary functions called via P/Invoke from C#.
findings.problem: 34 native .cpp files allocate std::vector, std::u16string, or std::wstring inside noexcept functions without try/catch(...), which calls std::terminate() on allocation failure. ArtworkFrameDetector::EdgeSupport divides by (end - start) without checking end > start (producing NaN on small thumbnails), and vn_input_read_left_click / vn_win32_keyboard_hook_install leave out parameters uninitialized on early returns.
findings.fix: Wrap throwing STL allocations in try { ... } catch (...) { return VN_ERR_FAIL; }, guard if (end <= start) return 0.0; in ArtworkFrameDetector.cpp:25, add ComScope to ShellIcons.cpp, and zero-initialize all out parameters at function entry.
findings.consequenceIfSkipped: Memory pressure or large clipboard/input payloads crash the app via std::terminate(), and small album art produces NaN frame scores.

findings.title: Rapidly copying Personal vault items strands decrypted files in temp storage, and importing duplicate items corrupts attachment counts
findings.whatThisIs: The clipboard history controller and store that manage encrypted Personal files and .vnotch-clipboard backup imports.
findings.problem: CopyAsync and CopyManyAsync assign _clipboardExportPaths = exported after await WriteClipboardAsync(data) outside _clipboardWriteGate, stranding decrypted Personal files on rapid copy. ClipboardHistoryStore.ImportCore overwrites duplicate.FileCount/SizeBytes with staged counts before deleting staging in finally, and ExtractPersonalDirectory misses zip directory entries ending with '\'.
findings.fix: Clean up and update _clipboardExportPaths inside _clipboardWriteGate, preserve duplicate.FileCount/SizeBytes in ImportCore, and check string.IsNullOrEmpty(entry.Name) in ExtractPersonalDirectory.
findings.consequenceIfSkipped: Decrypted private files accumulate in plaintext temp folders, and importing a backup can break existing clipboard attachments or fail on Windows-created zip files.

findings.title: Strict Local-Only Mode (Offline Mode) is bypassed by direct URL launches, and HTML drag-and-drop can fetch localhost URLs
findings.whatThisIs: External link launching in Settings/Integrity dialogs and remote image fetching when dragging HTML into the notch.
findings.problem: TranslationModelDetails_Click and AppIntegrityService.OpenOfficialRepo call Process.Start directly instead of SafeLauncher.TryOpenUrl, bypassing NetworkPrivacy in Strict Local-Only Mode. ClipboardDropReader.ResolveAsync downloads URLs from dropped HTML without blocking localhost or RFC1918 private IPs (SSRF), and AppIntegrityService.VerifyChecksumAsync leaks HttpResponseMessage instances.
findings.fix: Route both URL launches through SafeLauncher.TryOpenUrl, wrap HttpResponseMessage in using var, and reject loopback/private/link-local IP addresses in ClipboardDropReader.
findings.consequenceIfSkipped: Offline mode leaks outbound requests, dropped HTML can probe local services on 127.0.0.1, and failed browser launches can crash the Settings window.

findings.title: uninstall.exe ships without locale files, shows raw localization keys, and aborts before cleanup if VNotch.Native.dll is missing
findings.whatThisIs: The standalone uninstall.exe binary and the built-in --uninstall flow in V-Notch.exe.
findings.problem: Uninstall.csproj links LocalizationService.cs without embedding ..\Locales\*.json, so every message box displays raw keys like 'uninstall.confirmMessage'. Also, ResolveInstallDirectory() in Uninstall\Program.cs:56 runs outside TrySilently before StopRunningInstances and RemoveAppData, so a missing VNotch.Native.dll aborts the uninstaller before cleanup.
findings.fix: Embed ..\Locales\*.json into Uninstall.csproj, wrap ResolveInstallDirectory() in try/catch, release COM shortcut RCW in SetupOperations.cs, and unify the two uninstall implementations.
findings.consequenceIfSkipped: Users see broken key names when uninstalling, and partially deleted installs cannot be uninstalled cleanly.

findings.title: 'Reveal in Explorer' fails on file paths containing spaces or commas, and SafeLauncher reports false failures when a browser is already open
findings.whatThisIs: The Spotlight action that highlights a file in Windows Explorer and the helper that opens web links and Windows Settings pages.
findings.problem: SpotlightLauncher.TryRevealInExplorer calls startInfo.ArgumentList.Add($"/select,{item.Target}"), which quotes the whole argument as "/select,C:\My Folder\file.txt" when the path has spaces, breaking explorer.exe's custom parser. SafeLauncher.LaunchValidatedUri returns process != null, which is false whenever UseShellExecute = true hands a URL to an already-running browser.
findings.fix: Set startInfo.Arguments = $"/select,\"{item.Target}\"" in TryRevealInExplorer, and return true when Process.Start(psi) completes without throwing when psi.UseShellExecute is true.
findings.consequenceIfSkipped: 'Reveal in Explorer' fails for any file in folders with spaces, and callers of SafeLauncher falsely treat successful browser opens as failures.

findings.title: A single D3DImage.TryLock(5ms) timeout during display recovery leaves the Liquid Glass surface permanently blank
findings.whatThisIs: The Direct3D 9Ex / D3D11 shared-surface presenter that displays the blurred Liquid Glass backdrop inside WPF.
findings.problem: When AttachBackBuffer() is called after a front-buffer/display reset, if _image.TryLock(5ms) returns false, _attachedSurface is neither cleared nor retried. Later calls to PresentPendingFrame() see _attachedSurface == _renderSurface and skip SetBackBuffer forever.
findings.fix: Reset _attachedSurface = IntPtr.Zero and call ScheduleRetry() whenever _image.TryLock returns false inside AttachBackBuffer().
findings.consequenceIfSkipped: Locking/unlocking Windows, switching monitors, or GPU driver resets can leave the notch backdrop transparent or black until app restart.

findings.title: Always-on CompositionTarget.Rendering handlers keep the UI thread waking at 60–240 Hz even when idle
findings.whatThisIs: The per-VSync WPF rendering callbacks for Liquid Glass, desktop edge reveal, and the music visualizer.
findings.problem: MainWindow and D3DImageFramePresenter keep CompositionTarget.Rendering subscribed 24/7 even when idle; DisableSpotlightGlass() never unsubscribes; PromoteFromDesktopLayer overwrites _desktopTransparentFrameHandler without detaching the prior handler; and MusicVisualizer runs FFT math every frame without drawing after _copiedFeedback settles.
findings.fix: Subscribe to CompositionTarget.Rendering only while frames/animations are active, detach handlers in DisableSpotlightGlass() and PromoteFromDesktopLayer(), and call StopRendering() in MusicVisualizer when _copiedFeedback <= 0.005.
findings.consequenceIfSkipped: WPF's render loop wakes the CPU and GPU 60–240 times per second 24/7 even when the notch is collapsed and idle.

findings.title: Dragging the White Noise volume bar writes to disk synchronously on the UI thread on every mouse pixel, and media volume drags spawn unserialized thread-pool writes
findings.whatThisIs: The interactive volume sliders for White Noise and system/media playback inside the expanded notch.
findings.problem: WhiteNoiseStrip.SetVolumeFromMouse sets WhiteNoiseService.Volume on every MouseMove, which synchronously writes and moves white-noise.json on the UI thread at 125–1000 Hz. MainWindow.Controls.cs queues raw ThreadPool.QueueUserWorkItem calls on every volume drag instead of using _mediaVolumeWrites.
findings.fix: Debounce WhiteNoiseService.SaveState() asynchronously, subscribe WhiteNoiseStrip to Loc.LanguageChanged, and route MainWindow.Controls.cs volume writes through _mediaVolumeWrites.Schedule(...).
findings.consequenceIfSkipped: Dragging the White Noise slider stutters on disk I/O, and fast media volume drags jitter as out-of-order COM writes land.

findings.title: Cancelled WPF animation Completed callbacks fire and hide or reset active UI elements
findings.whatThisIs: Transition animations for media views, audio mixer panels, timer overlays, sliders, and Spotlight AI panels.
findings.problem: Replacing or clearing a WPF animation immediately fires the old animation's Completed event. Without a version counter check, interrupting a fade-out with a fade-in runs the old fade-out's cleanup callback and collapses the newly shown panel.
findings.fix: Increment a per-element transition version counter before starting each animation and return early in Completed if the counter has changed.
findings.consequenceIfSkipped: Rapidly toggling panels, tracks, or tabs leaves media controls, audio panels, or AI views invisible or stuck mid-transition.

findings.title: Unbounded caches, overlap timers, and undisposed native handles degrade multi-day uptime
findings.whatThisIs: Background monitoring, media metadata caching, Bluetooth polling, and logging services that run for the life of the tray app.
findings.problem: MediaSessionState dictionaries and MediaMetadataLookupService._failedLookups grow without bound; VideoIdCache.Put evicts only 1 item when inserting 2; BluetoothMonitorService and NotchModuleBase allow overlapping async timer ticks; GpuMonitorService.DisableNvml frees nvml.dll without synchronizing with the polling task; and RuntimeLog never closes _writer.
findings.fix: Cap cache sizes in MediaSessionState and MediaMetadataLookupService, use a while loop in VideoIdCache eviction, gate BluetoothMonitorService and NotchModuleBase ticks against re-entrancy, synchronize DisableNvml with _pollGate, and close RuntimeLog._writer on exit.
findings.consequenceIfSkipped: Over days of continuous playback and tray uptime, memory usage creeps up, Bluetooth state can desync, and GPU fallback can fault on an unloaded NVML DLL.

findings.title: Streaming AI responses re-parse the entire Markdown document on every word (O(W^2)), ElasticSlider allocates animations per mouse pixel, and FastBlurService overflows 32-bit math at large radii
findings.whatThisIs: The Spotlight AI streaming view, interactive elastic slider control, and native box-blur / weather / string truncation kernels.
findings.problem: OnAiStreamTimerTick rebuilds the entire FlowDocument from scratch every 20 ms word tick (O(W^2)). ElasticSlider allocates two DoubleAnimation objects per mouse pixel during drag. FastBlurService overflows 32-bit uint32_t / AVX2 multiplication at radius >= 33,025. WeatherService::RoundTemperature casts NaN/Infinity to int32_t (UB). SpotlightChatStore and WindowsSearchProvider split UTF-16 surrogate pairs at fixed truncation boundaries.
findings.fix: Incrementally append streamed AI words and rebuild Markdown at stream completion; set ElasticSlider Value directly during drag; cap FastBlurService::kMaxRadius to 256; check std::isfinite in RoundTemperature; and avoid splitting UTF-16 high surrogates on truncation.
findings.consequenceIfSkipped: Long AI answers lag the UI as they stream, slider drags churn GC, and extreme blur radii or NaN weather values produce corrupted output.

findings.title: 16 non-UI production files over 150 lines have zero direct unit tests
findings.whatThisIs: Core state, media, currency parsing, window Z-order, and surface binding services.
findings.problem: High-risk state and parsing files like SpotifyCanvasClient.cs (206L), WhiteNoiseService.cs (210L), ZOrderManager.cs (214L), MediaSessionState.cs (171L), SelectedPrice.cs / TranslationCurrencies (169L), and LiquidGlassSurfaceBinder.cs (292L) have no direct unit tests.
findings.fix: Add targeted unit tests for WhiteNoiseService start/stop lifecycle, MediaSessionState eviction bounds, TranslationCurrencies price extraction, and PlatformDetector/MediaHeuristics Hangul buffer expansion.
findings.consequenceIfSkipped: Regressions in audio thread lifecycle, currency parsing, and media state caching will continue to slip into releases.

findings.title: Heavy NuGet packages (AngleSharp, YoutubeExplode), 47 unused native exports, dead files, and ~1,300 lines of duplicated Liquid Glass and uninstall code
findings.whatThisIs: Third-party HTML/YouTube libraries, unused C#/C++ helpers, and duplicated window backdrop and installer code.
findings.problem: AngleSharp is bundled solely for a 15-line <a href> scan in SoundCloudMatching.cs; YoutubeExplode is bundled only for a 14-line fallback in YouTubeSubtitleService.cs even though FetchViaInnertubeAsync is already implemented; Debouncer.cs/cpp, ShelfViewportVirtualizer.cs/cpp, and 47 VN_EXPORT functions have zero production callers; and MainWindow.LiquidGlass.cs + SpotlightWindow.LiquidGlass.cs duplicate ~1,100 lines of capture/D3D host glue.
findings.fix: Move SoundCloud <a href> extraction into Native/Services/SoundCloudMatching.cpp and drop AngleSharp and YoutubeExplode; delete Debouncer.*, ShelfViewportVirtualizer.*, dead methods, and unused native exports; extract a shared LiquidGlassWindowHost; and remove stray root files.
findings.consequenceIfSkipped: Slower builds, larger single-file publish size, and bug fixes that must be applied twice across MainWindow and SpotlightWindow.

findings.title: Pass 1 fix regressions: OnRetryTick permanently unhooks Liquid Glass rendering, Timer fade-out collapses active Timer view, and duplicate clipboard imports overwrite PrimaryExtension
findings.whatThisIs: Three regressions introduced during Pass 1 remediation in D3DImageFramePresenter, MainWindow.Timer, and ClipboardHistoryStore.
findings.problem: D3DImageFramePresenter.OnRetryTick() calls CompositionTarget.Rendering -= OnRendering;, permanently detaching VSync after a single 5ms TryLock contention. MainWindow.Timer.cs sets TimerContent.Visibility = Collapsed before checking if (_isTimerView) return;. ClipboardHistoryStore.ImportCore overwrites duplicate.PrimaryExtension from staged files that are deleted in finally.
findings.fix: Remove CompositionTarget.Rendering -= OnRendering; from OnRetryTick() and call AttachBackBuffer() if _attachedSurface == IntPtr.Zero; move if (_isTimerView) return; to the top of both Timer Completed lambdas; and preserve duplicate.PrimaryExtension in ImportCore.
findings.consequenceIfSkipped: Any single D3D lock contention freezes the Liquid Glass backdrop, switching rapidly back to Timer view leaves it invisible, and duplicate clipboard imports lose file extension metadata.

findings.title: Lookbehind across cursor in SensitiveDataScrubber underflows size_t to SIZE_MAX inside noexcept and crashes the process
findings.whatThisIs: The native C++26 scrubber that redacts API keys, tokens, and secrets from logs and clipboard text.
findings.problem: try_read_scrub_standalone_token checks index >= 2 ("sk-") and index >= 3 ("enc:") without checking index - 2 >= cursor, which can set start.value_index < cursor and underflow static_cast<size_t>(value - cursor) to SIZE_MAX inside noexcept vn_sensitive_data_scrub, calling std::terminate(). Also try_read_scrub_field scans backwards past cursor into already-redacted values.
findings.fix: Bound all backward scans in try_read_scrub_field and try_read_scrub_standalone_token by cursor, and wrap vn_sensitive_data_scrub in try { ... } catch (...) { return VN_ERR_FAIL; }.
findings.consequenceIfSkipped: Malformed or adjacent token strings in logs or clipboard items crash V-Notch via std::terminate().

findings.title: Stopping the camera while StartAsync is initializing leaves _starting = true forever, permanently bricking the webcam
findings.whatThisIs: The MediaCapture webcam controller and frame dispatcher for the notch camera mirror.
findings.problem: TryBeginGracefulStop increments _fadeToken without resetting _starting = false while StartAsync is initializing, so StartAsync's finally block (if (startToken == _fadeToken) _starting = false;) skips resetting _starting, leaving _starting = true forever. Also StopCameraPreviewSafe resets _cameraFrameDispatchPending = false while a BeginInvoke callback is still queued.
findings.fix: Track _startToken separately from _fadeToken (and set _starting = false inside TryBeginGracefulStop), and only clear _cameraFrameDispatchPending inside the BeginInvoke callback's finally block.
findings.consequenceIfSkipped: Closing the notch while the camera is warming up permanently disables the camera until V-Notch is restarted.

findings.title: Pausing a media player that emits a single paused SMTC snapshot leaves ProgressEngine in Playing state forever
findings.whatThisIs: The media timeline interpolation and playback state engine that drives the notch progress bar.
findings.problem: ProcessPendingPauseConfirmation sets _pendingPauseConfirmation = true and _isPlaying = false and returns true, causing HandlePausedSnapshot to return early without setting _state = ProgressState.Paused. GetUiFrame() never expires _pendingPauseConfirmation after PauseConfirmationWindow (700ms).
findings.fix: Expire _pendingPauseConfirmation in GetUiFrame() once nowUtc - _pendingPauseStartedUtc >= PauseConfirmationWindow by setting _pendingPauseConfirmation = false; _state = ProgressState.Paused;, and require _isPlaying in RequiresPositionUpdates.
findings.consequenceIfSkipped: Pausing media leaves the internal state as Playing and keeps the UI progress timer ticking continuously in the background while paused.

findings.title: Audio Mixer volume and mute controls modify expired or inactive sessions instead of the active audio stream for multi-session apps
findings.whatThisIs: The per-application WASAPI audio session enumeration and volume/mute control in the Audio Mixer.
findings.problem: AudioMixerService.GetSessions locks in the first non-expired session per PID even if Inactive, while vn_audio_set_session_volume and vn_audio_toggle_session_mute in AudioSessions.cpp do not skip AudioSessionStateExpired (2) and return after modifying only the first matching session.
findings.fix: In AudioSessions.cpp, skip AudioSessionStateExpired and apply volume/mute changes to all non-expired sessions matching process_id; in AudioMixerService.cs, prefer AudioSessionStateActive (1) over Inactive (0).
findings.consequenceIfSkipped: Dragging an app's volume slider or clicking mute in the Audio Mixer has no effect on the active audio stream when the app has multiple WASAPI sessions.

findings.title: _thumbCts use-after-dispose race, background mutation of live MediaInfo, and silent truncation of SessionInstanceKey
findings.whatThisIs: The central GSMTC / browser media detection service and its native C++26 session key builder.
findings.problem: _thumbCts is leaked without Dispose() at lines 2517/2600, synchronously disposed at lines 1376/1434/1460 while background tasks register on token (throwing ObjectDisposedException), and not cancelled on Stop(); FetchYouTubeThumbnailAsync mutates live MediaInfo without _updateLock; and vn_media_detection_build_session_instance_key truncates the |<IUnknown hex> suffix when source_app_len >= out_cap - 1 - hex_len.
findings.fix: Let each thumbnail task dispose its own CTS in finally, cancel _thumbCts in StopCoreAsync, clone/lock MediaInfo on background mutation, and return VN_ERR_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL in vn_media_detection_build_session_instance_key when out_cap < source_app_len + 1 + hex_len.
findings.consequenceIfSkipped: Rapid track switches throw ObjectDisposedException, background thumbnail tasks race with UI readers of MediaInfo, and long AUMIDs collide across sessions.

findings.title: A single NaN audio sample from WASAPI loopback permanently poisons FFT and visualizer bar heights
findings.whatThisIs: The C++26 FFT, beat detection, and spring-smoothing DSP pipeline for the music visualizer.
findings.problem: DecodeSampleAt copies float samples without checking std::isfinite(value). A single NaN sample infects the FFT, bypasses std::max(NaN, 1e-9) and std::clamp(NaN, 0.0, 1.0) in NormalizeAmplitude, permanently NaN-poisons VnVisualizerDspState and bar heights, and invokes UB in static_cast<int32_t>(std::floor(t * noise_rate)).
findings.fix: Sanitize non-finite samples to 0.0f in DecodeSampleAt, guard !std::isfinite(amplitude) in NormalizeAmplitude and GetAudioReactiveRhythmAt, and validate 5-element array lengths in VisualizerDsp.cs.
findings.consequenceIfSkipped: Any momentary audio driver glitch containing a NaN float sample permanently breaks the music visualizer until app restart.

findings.title: Unclamped crop_size and missing dimension/NaN guards in SmartThumbnailCropService produce invalid Int32Rects and background Dispatcher leaks
findings.whatThisIs: The ONNX + C++26 smart album-art / thumbnail cropping service.
findings.problem: TryDetectTextCropRect and BuildCropRect do not clamp crop_size <= std::min(img_width, img_height), returning out-of-bounds VnCropRects that throw ArgumentException in WPF CroppedBitmap; GetCenterWeight divides by 0 on zero dimensions; ApplyNms violates std::stable_sort strict weak ordering on NaN; and TryGetPortraitCropAsync forgets resized.Freeze() and gray.Freeze() on a background thread.
findings.fix: Clamp crop_size in BuildCropRect, validate img_width > 0 && img_height > 0 in all vn_smartcrop_* exports, order NaN deterministically in ApplyNms, and Freeze() bitmaps in TryGetPortraitCropAsync.
findings.consequenceIfSkipped: Small thumbnails or text-heavy artwork can throw ArgumentException during cropping, and portrait cropping leaks thread-local WPF Dispatchers.

findings.title: std::clamp(NaN, ...) float-to-integer Undefined Behavior, integer overflow, and unaligned uint64_t* reads in C++ controllers and color extraction
findings.whatThisIs: The native C++26 math routines for Dynamic Island color extraction, calendar scroll physics, progress interpolation, timer formatting, and frame hashing.
findings.problem: HslToColor, GetAdaptiveBlurOpacity, vn_calendar_*, and vn_progress_interpolate_ticks cast floats to integers without std::isfinite checks; ComputeBrightnessDim loops buf_len / 4 instead of pixel_count; vn_timer_compute_adjust_ticks and vn_progress_format_time overflow int64_t/int32_t; and vn_glass_frame_hash_128 dereferences unaligned const uint64_t*.
findings.fix: Guard std::isfinite before float-to-int casts, bound ComputeBrightnessDim by std::min(pixel_count, buf_len / 4), clamp ticks before arithmetic, and use std::memcpy in vn_glass_frame_hash_128.
findings.consequenceIfSkipped: Non-finite playback rates or scroll values trigger C++ Undefined Behavior (INT_MIN), and rented buffers larger than pixel_count * 4 skew brightness dimming.

findings.title: Clicking the media widget runs synchronous cross-process UIAutomation on the UI thread (bypassing browser URL inspection consent), and PiP detection thrashes its cache on every poll
findings.whatThisIs: The browser media tab activator and the desktop window/PiP scanner.
findings.problem: MediaWindowActivator.InspectBrowserWindowTabs and TryGoBackInMediaTab run UIAutomation across browser windows synchronously on the WPF UI thread without checking WindowTitleScanner.IsBrowserUrlInspectionAllowed(). Also MediaDetectionService calls IsPipActive(procName) then IsPipActive(null), thrashing WindowTitleScanner's single-slot _lastPipProcessName cache on every poll.
findings.fix: Gate browser tab UIA inspection on WindowTitleScanner.IsBrowserUrlInspectionAllowed(), and cache global PiP scan results in WindowTitleScanner so IsPipActive(procName) and IsPipActive(null) do not invalidate each other.
findings.consequenceIfSkipped: Clicking the media widget when a browser is busy freezes the UI, browser tab inspection runs without consent, and every browser media poll runs double EnumWindows scans.

findings.title: PrivacyIndicatorService invokes StateChanged while holding _lifecycleLock, races on _microphoneActivityGate, and fails to restart its mic worker after an empty candidate list
findings.whatThisIs: The background service that monitors webcam and microphone usage across Windows processes.
findings.problem: PublishSnapshotToUi -> ApplyScanResult fires StateChanged while holding _lifecycleLock, resets _microphoneActivityGate._lastSignalUtc without _micFlowGate, and StartMicrophoneFlowWorkerLocked does not check !_micFlowTask.IsCompleted when restarting the worker after it exits on candidates.Count == 0.
findings.fix: Check _micFlowTask is { IsCompleted: false } in StartMicrophoneFlowWorkerLocked, raise StateChanged outside _lifecycleLock in PublishSnapshotToUi, and make _microphoneActivityGate._lastSignalUtc atomic via Interlocked.
findings.consequenceIfSkipped: Once microphone candidates temporarily drop to zero while the mic is active, active audio flow probing stops working until a full stop/start cycle occurs.

findings.title: Pausing during the 150ms pre-roll window permanently freezes the Spotify Canvas loop, and expanding a section in AudioMixerView fails to update AudioScrollViewer.Height
findings.whatThisIs: The dual-MediaElement Spotify Canvas video loop presenter and the expandable Audio Mixer view.
findings.problem: SpotifyCanvasPresenter.SetPlaybackState(false) does not reset _isSwapping = false when paused during the 150ms pre-roll window, freezing the Canvas loop on resume, and Hide()/Release() do not increment _sourceVersion. AudioMixerView.AnimateSectionToggle resizes the notch without updating AudioScrollViewer.Height, and Dispose() leaks _audioWrites.
findings.fix: Call StopLoopMonitoring() in SetPlaybackState(false) and increment _sourceVersion in Hide()/Release(); update AudioScrollViewer.Height in AnimateSectionToggle and dispose _audioWrites in AudioMixerView.Dispose().
findings.consequenceIfSkipped: Pausing near the end of a Canvas loop freezes the video, and expanding a collapsed Audio Mixer section clips sliders inside a tiny scroll box.

findings.title: Unguarded animation Completed callbacks and delayed state updates in MainWindow.*, CalendarPresenter, CountdownView, ClipboardTray, and SettingsWindow
findings.whatThisIs: Animation completion callbacks and lifecycle cleanup across MainWindow, CalendarPresenter, CountdownView, ClipboardTray, SettingsWindow, and LyricsService.
findings.problem: ShowLyricsPlaceholder, AnimateModeTransition, ApplyNotchVisibilityState, CountdownView, ClipboardTray.OnImportProgress, and SettingsWindow.CollapseCollapsibleRow lack generation/state guards on completion callbacks; CalendarPresenter defers _refs.MonthText.Text until fadeOut.Completed; PerformCleanup() does not unsubscribe BlockGreetingInput or dispose _youtubeSubtitleService; and LyricsService parses unbounded HTTP response streams.
findings.fix: Add generation/state guards to all 6 completion callbacks, track _targetMonthText immediately in CalendarPresenter, clean up BlockGreetingInput and _youtubeSubtitleService in PerformCleanup(), reuse a single recovery timer in ScheduleMediaBackgroundRecovery, and bound LyricsService streams to 512 KB.
findings.consequenceIfSkipped: Seeking songs blanks out the current lyric line, flicking the calendar across month boundaries shows the wrong month, and rapid toggles corrupt UI visibility.

findings.title: Remaining Pass 1 T-17/T-18 items not yet applied in GpuMonitorService, BluetoothMonitorService, MediaMetadataLookupService, PerformanceDiagnosticService, RuntimeLog, and SpotlightWindow.Ai
findings.whatThisIs: Six service stability and UI streaming items from Pass 1 (T-17 and T-18) verified as still unapplied in PONYTAIL_REVIEW.md.
findings.problem: GpuMonitorService.DisableNvml still frees nvml.dll without _pollGate; BluetoothMonitorService still allows overlapping refreshes; MediaMetadataLookupService still leaves _failedLookups unbounded and HttpResponseMessage undisposed; PerformanceDiagnosticService.cs:375 leaks Process.GetCurrentProcess(); RuntimeLog lacks shutdown flush/close; and SpotlightWindow.Ai.cs rebuilds the full Markdown FlowDocument on every word (O(W^2)).
findings.fix: Apply the remaining T-17 and T-18 fixes documented in AGENT_REMEDIATION_TASKS.md.
findings.consequenceIfSkipped: Multi-day tray sessions leak Process handles and HttpResponseMessage instances, risk NVML unload crashes, and stutter during long Spotlight AI streaming responses.
